title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police wrongly used AI facial recognition to link her to bank fraud. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota on four theft and four identity information charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million, saying police relied on a flawed facial recognition match from a fake ID and did not establish probable cause. She says she lost her home, car, and belongings, and was denied medications and dentures while in custody. The city declined to comment on pending litigation, and the lawsuit seeks accountability and better police training on facial recognition technology.
